headnotes.la: …nulli viri illustres, qui postpositis mundi illecebris tunc temporis eo in loco monasticam vitam ducebant; quin et *Gonthardi judicatus,* supra in Willelmi instrumento laudatus, ab Henrico confirmatur
headnotes.en: … who, having set aside the enticements of the world, at that time led the monastic life in that place; nay, even *Gonthard's adjudication,* praised above in William's instrument, is confirmed by Henry

headnotes.la: … monasterii benefactores recenset Otthonem Willelmum, nostri Willelmi consanguineum, ut supra diximus, cujus complures exstant chartae in Benigniani sicut et in Fructuariensis monasterii favorem datae
headnotes.en: …f the monastery he reckons Otto William, the kinsman of our William, as we said above, of whom there are extant several charters given in favor both of the Benignian and of the monastery of Fruttuaria

headnotes.la: Sub finem enumerat cellas, seu prioratus, qui jam tunc a monasterio illo pendebant; scilicet cellam
headnotes.en: Toward the end he enumerates the cells, or priories, which already then were dependent on that monastery; namely the cell

headnotes.la: Anno Christi 1023, aliud item privilegium ab eodem imperatore obtinuit Willelmus quo monasterium Fructuariense,
headnotes.en: In the year of Christ 1023, William obtained likewise another privilege from the same emperor, whereby he takes the monastery of Fruttuaria —

headnotes.la: sub speciali sua defensione suscipit, ac privilegium Benedicti VIII confirmat
headnotes.en: — under his special defense, and confirms the privilege of Benedict VIII

headnotes.la: Observat Hugo abbas Flaviniacensis in Chronico Virdunensi Willelmum nostrum, quem
headnotes.en: Hugh, abbot of Flavigny, observes in the *Chronicle of Verdun* that our William, whom he calls

headnotes.la: appellat, beato Henrico acceptissimum fuisse. Et paulo inferius eumdem Willelmum
headnotes.en: was most acceptable to blessed Henry. And a little below he says that the same William

headnotes.la: …psius charta patet, quae ab eodem Guichenone refertur, in qua Joannes ejusdem loci abbas memoratur, qui in Chronico Benigniano, supra, appellatur *Joannetinus* et Henricus, ejusque successores Augusti
headnotes.en: …enon, in which John, abbot of that same place, is mentioned — who in the Benignian Chronicle, above, is called *Joannetinus* — and Henry, and his successors the Augusti, are said to have been admitted

headnotes.la: … monasterii suo diplomate confirmavit anno 1070. Certe cum beatus Anno, ut refert Lambertus Schafnaburgensis, auctor aequalis, in Italia agens ad Fructuariense monasterium orationis causa divertisset,
headnotes.en: … in the year 1070. Certainly, when blessed Anno — as Lambert of Hersfeld, a contemporary author, relates — while acting in Italy had turned aside to the monastery of Fruttuaria for the sake of prayer,
